title: Genomic RNA Extraction by TRIzol Method Using Drosophila melanogaster Gut
author: Mohamed Sabeelil Islam
materials: discard the supernatant and retain the pellet

steps.title: Dissect and collect larval guts
steps.instruction: Dissect third‑instar Drosophila larvae and isolate the gut; collect approximately 10–15 guts.

steps.title: Add TRIzol and chloroform
steps.instruction: Place the dissected guts into a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube that already contains 200 µL TRIzol (to avoid spurt). Add an additional 600 µL TRIzol (total 800 µL, 0.8 mL). Then add 200 µL (0.2 mL) chloroform, vortex briefly, and incubate the mixture for 5 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Phase separation centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4 °C.

steps.title: Transfer aqueous phase and precipitate RNA
steps.instruction: Carefully transfer the upper aqueous phase (supernatant) to a new tube and add isopropanol in a volume equal to the transferred supernatant.

steps.title: RNA pellet centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tube at 12,000 × g for 10 minutes at 4 °C to pellet the RNA.

steps.title: Wash RNA pellet with ethanol
steps.instruction: Wash the RNA pellet twice with 1 mL cold 75 % ethanol. For each wash, add the ethanol, vortex the suspension, then centrifuge at 7,500 × g for 5 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 mL cold 75 % ethanol, vortex, centrifuge 7,500 × g for 5 min.
Repeat the ethanol wash a second time.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet and assess purity
steps.instruction: Discard the ethanol, retain the RNA pellet, add RNase‑free water to dissolve it, and check RNA purity (e.g., spectrophotometrically).
